subject: Question on extraction of log-likelihood during MCMC

messages.author: aea6b60b587ca006
messages.subject: Question on extraction of log-likelihood during MCMC
parts:
Hi Nimble devs and users!

I'm running MCMC for a hierarchical model with a large number (6000×7) of data nodes. Nimble's performance is great!

Let's call the data nodes "X" and their parent parameter nodes "Z".

I'd like to monitor the total log-likelihood of the parents nodes of the data nodes, or said otherwise, the total log-probability of the data conditional only on their "parent parameters", that is, log[p(X|Z)].

First I tried do to this by adding a monitor for "logProb_X", but this actually adds 6000×7 "logProb_X[...]" monitors – one for each scalar data variable; very unwieldy.

Then I tried by summing all "logProb_X[...]" within the model itself, but nimbleModel() warns me that "logProb_X" is not defined.

The manual explains the use of the RW_llFunction, but I don't think it applies in my case: I don't need to sample the log-likelihood, since it can be calculated exactly.

At last I inserted into the model a nimbleFunction that calculates the total log-likelihood and outputs it into a scalar node, and monitored that node. This works but it's prohibitively slow. I assume that Nimble's MCMC sampler already has, at each iteration, the values of the log-probabilities of the data log[p(X|Z)] (should be "logProb_X[...]"). So this third, slow approach above is doing something redundant by recalculating them.

Is it possible to somehow access the already calculated log-probabilities and sum them within the model, rather than having to monitor them and sum them at the end?

I hope I managed to explain my problem in an understandable way :)

Cheers!
Luca

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Question on extraction of log-likelihood during MCMC
parts:
Luca, I'm sorry this is very brief, but your easiest bet might be writing a custom sampler, which adds up all these logProbs and stores them into a (scalar) model node.  The run code of this sampler is essentially:

model$sum_logProbX <<- sum(model$logProb_X)

Then you'll also have to create the stochastic model node "sum_logProbX" in your model code, you could do this as a stochastic node node so it doesn't have a fixed deterministic value, e.g.

sum_logProbX ~ dnorm(0, 1)

Then, remove the default sampler added to this node "sum_logProbX", and add an instance of your custom sampler to the MCMC configuration.  Finally, make sure to add an MCMC monitor to sum_logProbX.

I think that would do it, fairly easily.  Let me know if any part of that doesn't make sense.

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: aea6b60b587ca006
messages.subject: setSamplers not reordering?
parts:
Dear Nimble devs,

I'm trying to use the setSamplers() method to reorder the execution of the samplers, but it doesn't seem to have any effect. As an example, let's say that

mcmcConf$printSamplers(executionOrder = TRUE)

gives me the samplers in the order x[1], x[2], y[1], y[2], and I'd like to have the ys sampled before the xs. I tried by giving the node names without indices, say

mcmcConf$setSamplers(c('y', 'x'))

and with explicit indices, say

mcmcConf$setSamplers(c('y[1]', 'y[2]', 'x[1]', 'x[2]'))

but in either case calling mcmcConf$printSamplers(executionOrder = TRUE) again shows that the sampling order has not changed.

Am I misunderstanding the use of setSamplers()? The manual says "Order can be modified by using setSamplers" in §7.9.1, but I may be misunderstanding here.

The example above is fictitious, but if needed I can give a minimal-code example.

This is for Nimble 0.12.1, the first version in which I've tried to use setSamplers.

Thank you for your help and for Nimble!
Luca

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: setSamplers not reordering?
parts:
Luca, indeed you are right, this is an oversight in a method used inside the MCMC configuration object, rooted in the method findSamplersOnNodes(), which is used internally to many of the configuration object methods.  You are right, in the instance of re-ordering the samplers using a vector of node names, that is:

conf$setSamplers(vector_of_node_names)

the ordering of the vector of node names is not respected.  This is not the advertised behaviour of setSamplers() method.  I'll take a look into a fix, which probably wouldn't be included in an official release for a while.    If it's helpful, I can point you to a GitHub branch including the fix (once I make it), but in the meantime, reordering the samplers instead using a *numeric* vector of sampler indices will work fine (which, by the way, originally was the only way of using the setSamplers() method, until support for character vectors of node names was subsequently "added").  Example:

mcmcConf$setSamplers(c(4, 3, 2, 1))

Please let me know if this works for you, and also whether sending you the "patched" branch would be helpful (once it's available).

Cheers,
Daniel

Please feel free to prioritize more urgent bugs and developments. I ended up simply specifying the samplers explicitly with addSampler(), in the order I want them, which is indeed respected by Nimble (and leading to much better results now). So this can wait :)

Thank you again for this amazing package with amazing support!
Luca
